source: CAMFAD student thesis: "Establishment of a New Coconut Plantation Farm", National School of Agriculture, July 1994
text:
Fertilizing: at planting, basal fertilizer supplying nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) is placed in the hole (roughly one handful), positioned under the backfill soil layer rather than directly against the roots; potassium (K) fertilizer is also used. Boron (B) is applied as a minor/micronutrient at a low rate, about 100 mg per tree per year, since boron deficiency can occur even though other micronutrients are often adequately supplied by local soil. Magnesium (Mg) deficiency is also noted as possible, recognizable by yellowing at the leaf tips, and can be corrected with MgSO4 (magnesium sulfate).

Weeding: weeds should be controlled regularly around young palms, roughly on a monthly basis during active growth, though less frequent weeding is acceptable where weed pressure is naturally low.

Intercropping along row spacing: on the open ground between coconut rows, farmers are advised they can grow companion/intercrop plants such as corn (ពោត), banana (ចេក), or beans (សណ្តែក) to make productive use of the land while the coconut canopy is still open. Intercrops should be kept at least 3-5 meters away from the coconut trunk so they do not compete directly with the palm's root zone.
